full_judgment:
Mr. Shahidul Islam J:- This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 19.7.2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Kurigram in other Appeal No. 21 of 2000 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 9.02.2000 passed by the Assistant Judge, Sadar. Kurigram in other Suit No 59 of 1993 decreeing the suit finally 

 2. By this Rule the plaintiff opposite party was called upon to show cause as to why the judgment and decree complained of in the Rule should not he set-aside and or pass such other or further order or orders be passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the predecessor of the petitioners No. 1-8 and the sole opposite party are 2(two) brothers. The petitioner No. 9 is the mother of the opposite party. The opposite party as plaintiff instituted other class suit No. 59 of 1993 in the court of Assistant Judge. Sadar, Kurigram seeking for a preliminary decree for partition to 1.001/4th acre stating interalia that the land under partition belonged to Dhaniullah, the father of the plaintiff. Said Dhaniullah transferred 2.25 acres of land in favour of his 2(two) sons the plaintiff and the defendant NO. 1. Thereafter he had only 20 acre of land and during his possession he (Dhaniullah) died leaving behind the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 as his sons and a widow the defendant No. 2. Thereafter the plaintiff sold .21 acre of land from Plot No. 1090 in favour of the defendant No. 1. The plaintiff demanded partition by mots and bounds and the same was refused and as such the suit. 

 5. The suit was decreed in preliminary for on admission by the parties, by the judgment and decree dated 26.9.94 by the Assistant Judge, Kurigram. 

 After passing of the preliminary decree the defendant made a prayer for final decree. A commissioner was appointed for effecting final allotment of saham who after making partition submitted report. The said report was accepted and the preliminary decree was made final by the judgment and decree dated 21.8.1996. 

 6. Against the said final decree the plaintiff preferred other Appeal NO. 86 of 1996 and the said appeal was allowed by the judgment and decree dated 28.4.97. The matter was sent back on remand for a fresh final partition decree. 

 8. The defendants submitted written objection against the said report but ultimately the said report was accepted and the final decree was passed by the judgment and decree dated 9.2.2000. 

 9. Being aggrieved by the said decree the defendant preferred other Appeal NO. 21 of 2000 and the said appeal was dismissed by the Joint District Judge by the impugned judgment and decree dated 19.7.2003. 

 10. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the defendants have moved this court and have obtained the instant Rule. 

 11. Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman, the learned advocate on appearing, before this court at the very outset drawn the attention of this court to the preliminary decree and pointed out that the preliminary decree was passed on admission made by the plaintiff and the defendants. He submitted that the defendants made a prayer for saham claiming their specific possession in .53 acre of land of Plot No. 843, 844 and 849 and also claimed possession in .20 acre of land adjacent to their homestead from Plot No. 850 and 855. He submitted that the plaintiff did not raise any objection against such a prayer for separate saham. He submitted that the trial court also considered that prayer and has specifically mengoned in the judgment dated 26.9.94 that “বিবাদী যেহেতু পৃথক ঠাহামের প্রার্থনা পূর্বক ১০০/- টাকার কোর্ট ফীস দাখিল করিয়াছেন। সেই হেতু বিবাদীগন ও তাহাদের দাবীকৃত ভূমি বাবদ (যেহেতু বাদীর আপত্তি নাই) পৃথক ছাহাম পাইতে পারেন” He submitted that in spite of that admission the learned advocate commissioner has allotted only .44 acre of land from Plot No. 443, 444 and 449 in the saham of defendants. He submitted that the advocate commissioner had no jurisdiction to go beyond the direction given in the preliminary decree. He further submitted that the defendants have prayed for saham claiming specific possession in the land of Plot No. 443, 444 and 449 and also in .20 acre of land of Plot No. 850 and 855 and the plaintiff has accepted that claim. He submitted that the learned advocate commissioner on violating the direction given in the preliminary decree has allotted the specifically possessed land of the defendant in the saham of the plaintiff. He submitted that both the courts below overlooked the said illegal distribution of saham made by the commissioner and passed the final decree. He submitted that the appellate court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in failing to consider that the admitted specific possession of the defendant and the specific direction of the trial court has been disturbed by the advocate commissioner in making final allotment of saham. 

 12. Mr. Abul Kashem, the learned advocate for the opposite party on the other hand submitted that the courts below on considering the evidence on record and also on considering the convenience of both the parties have accepted the final decree. He submitted that the judgment and decree impugned in the Rule being a judgment of affirmance, there is no scope to interfere with the same. 

 13. I have considered the submission made by the learned advocates of both the parties. I have perused the preliminary decree, the field book prepared by the advocate commissioner showing final allotment of saham and written objection filed against the final allotment of saham. I have also gone through the admission made by the PW1 in his evidence who did not raise any objection against the defendants prayer for saham to .53 acre of land of Plot No. 443. 444 and 449 which is their homestead and did not dispute for allotting .20 acre of land from Plot No. 850 and 855 from adjacent to the homestead of the defendant constructed upon the land on Plot NO. 443, .444 and 449. The plaintiff himself in his cross-examination also admitted that he has got no objection if the defendant is given saham to his exclusively possessed land from those plots. It appears from the saham chita that the defendant has not been alloted .53 acre of land from Plot No. 443, 444 and 449 and has not been allotted .20 acre of land from Plot No. 850 and 855. It appears from the saham chittar that .09 acre of land from Plot No. 449 has been allotted to the plaintiff which he is not entitled to get as per the preliminary decree. So it appears that the final decree impugned in the Rule has been passed violating admission made by the plaintiff himself in his evidence and also has been passed violating the specific direction given by the trial court in the preliminary decree. Both the courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in accepting the final decree. There is merit in this Rule. 

 14. In the result, this Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree dated 19.7.2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Kurigram in other Appeal No. 21 of 2000 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 9.2.2000 passed by the Assistant Judge, Sadar, kurigram in other Suit No. 59 of 1993 are set-aside. The suit is sent back on remand to the court of Assistant Judge, Kurigram directing him to issue a fresh writ to the advocate commissioner for effecting final partition as per the direction given in the preliminary decree and also as per the admission made by the plaintiff. The Assistant Judge. Kurigram is further-directed to mention specifically in the writ to allot .53 acre of land (homestead) to the defendant from Plot NO. 443, 444 and 449. The Assistant Judge is directed to complete the final decree proceeding within a period of 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of the record. The office is directed to. Send down the Record at once.
